file holds refers to guide models.yaml the litellm id each name calls, its type (llm or embedding), its params nothing Models rewards.yaml a catalog reward, its kwargs, which way is better models (a judge's model) Rewards datasets.yaml where rows come from, the Jinja templates over them, what answers them, the reward rewards, models, mcp_servers, environments Datasets mcp_servers.yaml MCP tool servers an agent dataset or an environment is given nothing MCP tools a2a_agents.yaml remote A2A agents an a2a sweep compares nothing A2A agents environments.yaml the Harbor sandboxes a harbor: dataset's agent works in mcp_servers Environments evaluations.yaml saved sweeps: which models on which datasets models, datasets, a2a_agents Evaluations leaderboards.yaml saved ways of ranking finished runs models, datasets Leaderboards

items.title: The rules every file follows
items.text:
• The file name decides the registry. Only <registry>.yaml is read, with that exact name and the .yaml extension. model.yaml, models.yml or my-datasets.yaml are ignored by a run; openarena check reports them as errors and gives the name to use.
  • One top-level key, the file's own. models.yaml holds models: only. Another registry's key in the same file is not read; check says which file to move it to.
  • A missing file is an empty registry. A workspace with no A2A agents can delete a2a_agents.yaml, or keep it as a2a_agents: {}. The template keeps every file so the commented field lists are at hand.
  • Names match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$, at most 128 characters: gpt-4o-mini, gsm8k-20.
  • References are by name, never by id. A dataset's reward is a rewards key; an evaluation's language_models are models keys; a judge's language_model is a models key. A litellm id such as openai/gpt-4o-mini appears once, in models.yaml. To switch a judge or a model version everywhere, you change one line.
  • Unknown fields are errors. A misspelled field is reported with the rename that fixes it (Checking configs). Nothing inside an entry is silently ignored.
  • A key written twice is an error. Plain YAML would keep the second one without a word; the engine refuses the file and gives the line.
  • tags are lowercase labels matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9:+./-]*$: [math, reasoning]. description is free text. Neither changes what runs; they are for listing and browsing.

Each file of a new workspace starts with a comment listing every field its entries take, with the optional ones as commented examples. Read it before editing: it is the quickest reference for that registry.

Why one file per registry

Each file changes for its own reason: adding a model touches models.yaml, a new benchmark touches datasets.yaml. Diffs stay small, two people rarely edit the same file, and openarena check configs/models.yaml checks one file against its neighbours.

items.title: What a run reads from them
items.text:
openarena evaluations run NAME does not run the whole folder. It takes the evaluation NAME and gathers only what it needs into one config:

  • the evaluation itself;
  • the datasets it lists;
  • the rewards, MCP servers and environments those datasets name, and the MCP servers those environments name;
  • for an a2a sweep, the A2A agents on its axis;
  • every model, since rewards and metrics name theirs by key too.

So a broken entry that the evaluation does not use does not stop the run. It still shows in openarena check, which reads every file. The gathered config is validated before the first model call: an unknown reference, a dataset with no reward, or a model of the wrong type stops the run with a message, before it costs anything.

items.title: tasks/ and environments/: the Harbor folders
items.text:
These two folders only matter for Harbor datasets, where an agent works in a sandbox. Delete them if you never run one.

folder what it is who uses it tasks/<task>/ a whole Harbor task: task.toml, instruction.md, environment/, tests/test.sh, solution/solve.sh a harbor_tasks dataset, through its config.path environments/<name>/environment/ the build context of the environment <name> in environments.yaml: whatever its Dockerfile copies a harbor: dataset over rows, through harbor.environment

Both are found beside configs/, not relative to where you run the command:

  • environments/<name>/ is looked up for each environment the evaluation uses.
  • A harbor_tasks dataset's relative path (the template's path: tasks) is read against the folder that holds configs/. An absolute path is read where it is, and is not copied.

At each run both are copied into the run folder, after deleting the previous copy. A run therefore uses the folders as they are now: a file you removed since the last run is gone from this one too.

init makes the .sh scripts executable

Harbor runs a task's scripts as they are. init sets the executable bit on every .sh it writes. A script you add yourself needs chmod +x.

items.title: Data files
items.text:
local and folder datasets read files from disk through their config.path. Unlike the Harbor folders, that path is used as written: a relative path is read from the folder you run the command in.

# ...
datasets:
  my-questions:
    type: local
    config:
      path: data/questions.jsonl     # relative to where you run openarena

Keep such files in a data/ folder at the workspace root and run commands from there. Then the paths in datasets.yaml work for everyone who clones the workspace. Use an absolute path only for data that lives outside the workspace on purpose (a shared drive, a large private file).

Datasets from a hub or a tracing platform (huggingface, langfuse, mlflow, ...) need no local files: they are fetched at run time, with the credentials in .env.

items.title: .env: keys and endpoints
items.text:
The registries never hold an API key: a model entry's params only take generation settings (temperature, max_tokens, reasoning_effort, and dimensions for embeddings). Keys and server addresses come from the environment, which keeps them out of git and lets each person use their own. A field that must carry a secret (a header, a server's env) names the variable with ${NAME} (Secrets in configs).

cp .env.template .env      # then uncomment and fill in what your models need

How it is loaded:

  • openarena evaluations run reads .env from the folder that holds configs/ (the parent of --configs), before anything else.
  • A variable already set in your shell wins: .env never overrides it.
  • No other command loads .env. check, list and leaderboards run make no model calls and need no keys; check only reads the file to look up the ${NAME} references a config holds.
  • The file is optional. Without one, the run uses your shell's environment.
setting comes from wins over your shell (export OPENAI_API_KEY=..., CI secrets) .env .env beside configs/ nothing; it only fills what the shell left unset

So a CI job or a one-off override (OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-other openarena evaluations run smoke) works without editing the file.

items.title: The variables
items.text:
ModelsHarborDataset sourcesTracing variable when you need it OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, MISTRAL_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, ... a hosted model: the key of each provider prefix in models.yaml, judges included OLLAMA_API_BASE ollama/... ids, when Ollama is not on http://localhost:11434 HOSTED_VLLM_API_BASE vllm/... ids: your server's OpenAI endpoint, ending in /v1

These are read by litellm, so any provider variable litellm knows works. Since a model entry takes no address of its own, there is one address per kind of local server, shared by every model of that kind.

variable what it does default ARENA_HARBOR_SANDBOX where trials run: a Harbor environment type (e2b, docker, daytona, modal, ...) e2b E2B_API_KEY E2B's key. Without it, the e2b setting falls back to the local Docker none ARENA_HARBOR_LOCAL_CPUS, ARENA_HARBOR_LOCAL_MEMORY_MB CPUs and memory a local Docker task gets when its environment sets none 2, 2048 ARENA_HARBOR_LOCAL_TRIALS trials at once on the local Docker 1 ARENA_HARBOR_WORKDIR where Harbor's task folders and trials go instead of the run folder the run's harbor/

An unknown ARENA_HARBOR_SANDBOX value stops the run with the list of known ones, rather than scoring every task 0.

variable for LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY, LANGFUSE_HOST langfuse datasets LANGSMITH_API_KEY, LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT langsmith datasets PHOENIX_API_KEY, PHOENIX_COLLECTOR_ENDPOINT (or PHOENIX_HOST and PHOENIX_PORT) phoenix datasets OPIK_API_KEY, OPIK_WORKSPACE, OPIK_URL_OVERRIDE opik datasets BRAINTRUST_API_KEY, BRAINTRUST_APP_URL, BRAINTRUST_ORG_NAME braintrust datasets MLFLOW_SOURCE_TRACKING_URI mlflow datasets that set no tracking_uri of their own UNITY_CATALOG_API_URL, UC_TOKEN, and the S3 settings S3_ENDPOINT, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION unity_catalog datasets

See Datasets for each provider's own fields.

variable what it does MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI the MLflow server runs are traced into; unset means no tracing ARENA_MLFLOW_TRACING 0, false, no or off turns tracing off while keeping the URI MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_NAME the experiment traces go to when no run names one

Tracing is optional; nothing in the workspace depends on it. The arena app traces its runs when the server answers, and an unreachable server leaves tracing off with a warning instead of slowing every call. openarena evaluations run itself does not switch tracing on in this version: its record is result.json.

items.title: Secrets in configs
items.text:
Some fields have to carry a secret: an A2A agent's or an MCP server's headers, a stdio server's or an environment's env. Write a reference to an environment variable there instead of the value, and put the value in .env:

a2a_agents:
  support-bot:
    url: https://support-agent.example.com
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer ${SUPPORT_BOT_TOKEN}"

# .env
SUPPORT_BOT_TOKEN=...
  • Any string value in any registry may hold ${NAME}. When a run reads its config (openarena evaluations run, and the arena app when it launches one), each reference is replaced by the variable, after .env is loaded, so the shell still wins over the file.
  • A variable that is not set makes the run refuse to start, before any call, naming each variable and where it is used.
  • The run's snapshot, .open-arena/<evaluation>/config.yaml, keeps the ${NAME} references, not the values, so it can be shared.
  • $${NAME} writes a literal ${NAME}. Jinja's {{ ... }} in templates is not touched.
  • openarena check looks each ${NAME} up in your shell and in the workspace's .env, and warns about one set in neither. It is a warning, not an error: CI can check configs without the secrets.

items.title: .open-arena/: the runs
items.text:
openarena evaluations run NAME writes everything into one folder per evaluation, <state-dir>/NAME/, with --state-dir defaulting to .open-arena in the folder you run from.

.open-arena/
  smoke/                        one folder per evaluation name
    config.yaml                 the evaluation and every entry it names, gathered: what ran
    result.json                 the scores, written when the sweep ends
    gsm8k-20/                   trial state of each dataset: what makes a run resume
    harbor/                     Harbor tasks, trials and trials.jsonl, for Harbor datasets
    environments/ tasks/        copies of the Harbor folders the run used
file why it is there what reads it config.yaml a snapshot of exactly what ran, rewritten at every run leaderboards run (to map names to model ids), you result.json the scores per model, dataset and metric leaderboards run, Reading results <dataset>/ each cell's trial, saved as it finishes the next run of the same evaluation, to resume harbor/ Harbor task folders, trials and their logs you, when a Harbor row fails

Two consequences of "one folder per evaluation name":

  • Running the same evaluation again resumes it. Finished cells are kept and only the missing or failed ones run. After changing what a finished cell depends on (a dataset, a model's params, a reward), add --no-cache, or the old cells are reused (Evaluations).
  • The latest run of an evaluation replaces the previous one's result.json. To keep both, copy the first away, save the second under another evaluation name, or run it into another --state-dir.

openarena leaderboards run reads every <state-dir>/*/result.json, newest first per cell, so every evaluation run into the same state dir feeds the same leaderboards. Point --state-dir elsewhere to rank a separate set of runs.

Avoid dataset names that clash with the run folder

Each dataset's trial state is a sub-folder named after it, beside harbor/, tasks/ and environments/. A dataset named harbor, tasks or environments would share a folder with them.

items.title: What lands outside the workspace
items.text:
A run also writes a few things elsewhere. They matter when you clean up or move a workspace.

  • Harbor on a snap-packaged Docker. That Docker cannot read hidden folders such as .open-arena, so Harbor's tasks, trials and temporary files go under ~/arena-harbor/ instead, one sub-folder per run. ARENA_HARBOR_WORKDIR moves them anywhere you choose. trials.jsonl stays in the run's harbor/ either way.
  • A default model. An evaluation's default_language_model or default_embedding_model is also saved in a per-user settings file in your home folder, as a side effect of setting it, and a later run that sets no default can inherit it. Give rewards and metrics their language_model explicitly when this matters.
  • --json FILE writes a copy of the result or ranking wherever you point it.

items.title: How the command finds everything
items.text:
There is no search up the folder tree and no global config file. Every path comes from two options and the folder you run in.

what where it is looked for change it with the registries ./configs --configs DIR .env the parent of the configs folder move the file, or export the variables tasks/, environments/ the parent of the configs folder an absolute harbor_tasks path, read in place local / folder data the folder you run in, for a relative path an absolute path runs ./.open-arena --state-dir DIR rows per batch the dataset's batch_size, overridden by the evaluation's --batch-size N, which overrides both Run from the workspace (recommended)Run from elsewhere 
cd my-arena
openarena check configs
openarena evaluations run smoke
openarena leaderboards run overall

Every default lines up: configs/, .env, the Harbor folders, data paths and .open-arena/ all resolve inside my-arena/.

openarena evaluations run smoke --configs my-arena/configs --state-dir my-arena/.open-arena
openarena leaderboards run overall --configs my-arena/configs --state-dir my-arena/.open-arena

.env and the Harbor folders still come from my-arena/, but runs go to ./.open-arena unless you pass --state-dir, and relative data paths are read from the current folder. Pass both options, and prefer absolute data paths, when a script or CI job runs from another folder.

items.title: Organising a workspace
items.text:
SoloTeamSeveral setups

One workspace, run from its root, one .env. Use evaluation names as the unit of work: smoke to check a setup on a few rows (limit: 5), then math-compare for the full run. Keep .open-arena/ out of git and treat it as a cache you can delete; what you keep is configs/ and, when you need a record, the result.json files.

One workspace in a shared repository, with configs/, the Harbor folders, the skills and .env.template committed. Each person keeps their own .env. A few habits keep it workable:

  • Add every key a run needs to .env.template, commented, so a new member sees what to set, the variables your configs name as ${NAME} included.
  • Prefix names by project or owner when several people add entries (team-a-gsm8k, judge-v2): a name is shared by the whole registry, and the same key written twice is an error.
  • Run openarena check configs in CI. It reads every file, needs no keys, and exits 1 on an error, so a broken reference never reaches the main branch.
  • Share results, not run folders. .open-arena/ holds trial state and Harbor logs that are large and tied to one machine. To rank everyone's runs together, collect each run's config.yaml and result.json into a shared folder laid out as <state-dir>/<evaluation>/, and point leaderboards run --state-dir at it. Give evaluations distinct names, or one person's run replaces another's.

The same registries against different endpoints (staging and production, say) are best kept as one workspace with the variables set in the shell, which wins over .env, or two env files you swap.

Genuinely different sets of registries can live side by side with --configs (configs/ and configs-nightly/ in one folder). They then share the same .env, tasks/ and environments/, since those are found beside the configs folder. When they need different ones, use separate workspaces.

items.title: Versioning
items.text:
The .gitignore that init writes:

# Keys and endpoints (copy .env.template)
.env

# Runs: configs snapshots, results, Harbor trials
.open-arena/

# Python
__pycache__/
*.py[cod]
.venv/

That covers the defaults. Extend it when you move things:

you use add to .gitignore --state-dir runs/... that folder --json results/... that folder, unless you commit results on purpose a second env file (.env.staging) that file large local data data/, or the files concerned

Commit .env.template, never .env. Commit CLAUDE.md as the link it is; on a system where links cannot be made, init writes it as a copy of AGENTS.md instead.

Committing results on purpose

To keep a record of a published comparison, commit that run's config.yaml and result.json only, for example under results/<evaluation>/. That pair says what ran and what it scored, and is all leaderboards run --state-dir results needs to rank it again. Leave out the dataset sub-folders and harbor/: they are trial state and logs.

items.title: For coding agents
items.text: AGENTS.md, its CLAUDE.md link and .agents/skills/ exist so that Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or another coding agent started in the folder knows the layout, the rules above and the commands to run. Keep them committed, and refresh the skills from a fresh init after an upgrade. See Coding agents.

items.title: What the example runs
items.text:
evaluation runs needs smoke qwen38 on gsm8k-20, 20 grade-school math questions, scored by exact match a local Ollama harbor gpt-4o-mini driving the terminus-2 agent on the hello-world task and on 5 GSM8K questions worked in a Python sandbox OPENAI_API_KEY, and Docker or E2B_API_KEY

And two leaderboards: overall (every model on every dataset, reward first) and math (GSM8K, the reward alone).

items.title: In the arena app
items.text: The layout is the arena's own: a workspace made by init is one the arena web app opens as it is, forms and all.

items.title: API reference
items.text:
openarena is a command and a Python package. Everything the command does is a function you can call: read and check a configs folder, run a sweep, rank its results.

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

from openarena.config.files import evaluation_config
from openarena.evaluate import run_sweep

raw = evaluation_config(Path("my-arena/configs"), "smoke")   # the evaluation and every entry it names
run = Path("runs/smoke")
run.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
(run / "config.yaml").write_text(yaml.safe_dump(raw, sort_keys=False))
result = asyncio.run(run_sweep(str(run / "config.yaml"), state_dir=run))
print(result["rows"])
page module what Configuration entries openarena.config.entries one model per registry entry Run configuration openarena.config a run's whole config, references resolved Checking openarena.config.check the problems of a registry, with their fixes Running a sweep openarena.evaluate run_sweep Leaderboards openarena.leaderboard gather results into a board, rank it Dataset providers openarena.datasets where rows come from Rewards openarena.rewards the reward catalog Harbor openarena.harbor Harbor tasks, agents and sandboxes

items.title: check_folder
items.text:
check_folder(configs: Path) -> list[Report]

check_file for each <registry>.yaml of configs, and a problem for any other YAML file there, which nothing reads.

items.title: check_file
items.text:
check_file(path: Path, *, beside: Path | None = None) -> Report

Every problem of the registry file path, <registry>.yaml, references checked against the registries in beside (its folder by default).

items.title: check_registry
items.text:
check_registry(section: str, entries: dict[str, Any], *, registries: dict[str, dict] | None = None) -> Report

Every problem of the section registry entries ({name: entry}), held in memory.

registries are the other registries by section ({"models": {name: entry}, ...}), the ones references are checked against; entries stands for its own section whatever registries holds. None checks no reference. A section registries lacks that section refers to is said once, as a warning. The report's path is None and its problems carry no line.

items.title: Report dataclass
items.text: Report(path: Path | None, section: str, names: list[str] = list(), problems: list[Problem] = list())

items.title: Problem dataclass
items.text: Problem(level: Literal['error', 'warning'], where: str, message: str, fix: str | None = None, line: int | None = None)

items.title: Config
items.text:
The full validated config.yaml.

Config.load(path) is the entry point — it parses YAML, validates, cross-checks every reference, and returns this object. The accessors below hand the sweep what it needs with the references resolved.

items.title: language_models property
items.text:
language_models: list[str]

The sweep axis, by name.

items.title: default_language_model property
items.text:
default_language_model: Any

The evaluation's default language model: its id, or the model built with its entry's params.

items.title: default_embedding_model property

default_embedding_model: Any

The evaluation's default embedding model: its id, or the model built with its entry's params.

items.title: metrics property
items.text:
metrics: list[MetricEntry]

The evaluation's metrics, added to every dataset's, their models resolved.

items.title: load classmethod
items.text:
load(path: str | Path) -> 'Config'

Parse + validate a YAML config file, each ${NAME} in it replaced by the environment variable (files.expand).

items.title: selected_dataset_names
items.text:
selected_dataset_names() -> list[str]

Datasets the sweep should run, in the evaluation's order.

items.title: model_id
items.text:
model_id(name: str) -> str

The litellm id an entry of the sweep axis calls: its models.<name>.model; an a2a sweep's axis is agent names, kept as they are.

items.title: lm_kwargs
items.text:
lm_kwargs(name: str) -> dict[str, Any]

Keyword arguments for LanguageModel(model=self.model_id(name), ...), or EmbeddingModel(...) for an embedding model.

Empty for a model with no params, in which case the program builders hand the framework the bare id.

items.title: dataset_entry
items.text:
dataset_entry(ds_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]

The flat mapping the dataset providers read (datasets.load_dataset_from_config).

items.title: resolved_agent
items.text:
resolved_agent(ds_name: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None

Per-dataset agent: block with mcp_servers: resolved against the top-level registry into {name: connection_dict} form (the shape MultiServerMCPClient(connections=...) expects). Returns None when the dataset uses a generator instead.

items.title: harbor_spec
items.text:
harbor_spec(ds_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]

A Harbor dataset's run: its block, and, over rows, its environment's entry and the MCP connections that environment names.

Over task folders (harbor_tasks), tasks is set and there is no environment: each task brings its own, and its own tests.

items.title: a2a_connection
items.text:
a2a_connection(name: str) -> dict[str, Any]

Where the A2A agent name on an a2a sweep's axis is: {url, headers, card_path, timeout_sec}.

items.title: reward_spec
items.text:
reward_spec(ds_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]

Reward spec ready for rewards.get(...): the dataset's reward entry, direction: stripped, models resolved.

An MCP agent answers with the schema's fields and its messages, the tool-calling transcript, which a target never carries; so a reward that sets no mask of its own gets out_mask: ["messages"], lest a reward comparing whole objects (exact_match) score every row 0. A Harbor trial answers with its whole ATIF trajectory, so such a reward reads its answer alone (in_mask: ["answer"]); the verifier's reward (SELF_SCORED) reads the trajectory's rewards. One that names masks is left as written, so a judge can be pointed at the steps on purpose.

items.title: dataset_metrics
items.text:
dataset_metrics(ds_name: str) -> list[MetricEntry]

Per-dataset metric entries (NOT merged with the evaluation's), their models resolved.

items.title: evaluation_config
items.text:
evaluation_config(configs: Path, name: str) -> dict

The config run_sweep reads for the evaluation saved as name in configs; see gather.

items.title: Dataset providers
items.text: A dataset's type picks one of these; its config is the provider's arguments, plus the templates and schemas every provider takes.

items.title: Dataset
items.text:
Dataset(input_data_model=None, input_schema=None, input_template=None, output_data_model=None, output_schema=None, output_template=None, batch_size=None, limit: int = None, repeat: int = 1, **kwargs)

Base class for streaming datasets compatible with the framework's trainers.

The framework's Trainer.fit/evaluate/predict(x=...) accepts a Python generator that yields (inputs,) or (inputs, targets) tuples — one tuple per batch. See the framework's generator data adapter and its data-adapter dispatch.

Subclasses implement _iter_rows() as a generator yielding raw row dicts (one per source example). The base class' __iter__ then renders each row through the Jinja2 templates, validates the shape, and yields batched (x, y) numpy object arrays — including the repeat expansion. Calling the dataset returns a fresh types.GeneratorType suitable for the framework:

program.evaluate(x=my_dataset())

The shape of the per-row input/target objects is controlled by either a Python DataModel class (input_data_model / output_data_model) OR a raw JSON Schema (input_schema / output_schema). The two are mutually exclusive on each side. With a class, rows are validated via cls.model_validate_json(rendered). With a schema, rows are wrapped as JsonDataModel(schema=..., json=json.loads(rendered)) — the schema flows directly into the LM as a structured-output constraint, so any JSON Schema feature (enum, const, oneOf, ...) is supported.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default input_data_model DataModel

Python class describing batch inputs. Defaults to ChatMessages in subclasses when neither this nor input_schema is provided.

None input_schema dict | str

Raw JSON Schema for batch inputs. May be given as a dict or as a JSON-encoded string. Mutually exclusive with input_data_model.

None input_template str

Jinja2 template string used to render raw rows into the input shape. Required.

None output_data_model DataModel

Python class describing batch targets. Defaults to ChatMessage when output_template is given but neither this nor output_schema is. Must be omitted when output_template is omitted.

None output_schema dict | str

Raw JSON Schema for batch targets. Mutually exclusive with output_data_model. Must be omitted when output_template is omitted.

None output_template str

Jinja2 template string used to render raw rows into the target shape. Optional — when omitted, the dataset is inputs-only and yields single-element (x,) batches (no targets). Rewards that need y_true will see it missing.

None batch_size int

Number of examples per yielded batch. None lets the subclass decide (or yield the whole dataset as one batch).

None limit int

Optional. Maximum number of raw (pre-repeat) examples to iterate over. None (default) means no cap. Useful for capping huge or streaming sources for quick experiments / smoke tests.

None repeat int

Number of consecutive copies to emit per raw example. Defaults to 1 (no expansion). Setting repeat == batch_size makes every batch a group of N rollouts of the same prompt — the expected layout for GRPO-style RL where reward statistics are computed across rollouts of one input.

1 **kwargs

Provider-specific fields forwarded by subclasses (e.g. HF dataset name, split, revision, API key, file path, ...).

{}

items.title: __iter__
items.text:
__iter__()

Render rows through the templates and yield batches.

Yields (x, y) when an output_template is configured, or single-element (x,) batches when it isn't. Honors limit (caps raw rows), repeat (each raw example is emitted repeat times in a row), and batch_size (size of the yielded numpy object arrays; None accumulates everything into a single trailing batch). The trailing partial batch is always flushed at the end.

items.title: __call__
items.text:
__call__()

Return a fresh generator over the dataset's batches.

items.title: __len__
items.text:
__len__()

Number of batches, if known. Override when the size is finite.

items.title: HuggingFaceDataset
items.text:
HuggingFaceDataset(path, *, name=None, split=None, revision=None, streaming=True, input_data_model=None, input_schema=None, input_template=None, output_data_model=None, output_schema=None, output_template=None, batch_size=1, limit: int = None, repeat: int = 1, **kwargs)

Streaming dataset backed by a HuggingFace datasets source.

Each row produced by datasets.load_dataset is rendered through the Jinja2 input_template / output_template to JSON, validated against the corresponding DataModel (or ChatMessages when None), and accumulated into batches of size batch_size. Each batch is yielded as (x, y) — numpy object arrays of DataModel instances — matching the format the framework's GeneratorDataAdapter expects.

Templates should render to JSON. Use Jinja's tojson filter for safe string escaping.

Example:

ds = HuggingFaceDataset(
    path="gsm8k",
    name="main",
    split="train",
    input_data_model=MathQuestion,
    input_template='{"question": {{ question | tojson }}}',
    output_data_model=NumericalAnswer,
    output_template='{"answer": {{ answer.split("####")[-1].strip() | tojson }}}',
    batch_size=8,
)
program.fit(x=ds())

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The HuggingFace dataset repo / builder name (first positional argument of datasets.load_dataset).

required name str

Optional. The dataset configuration name.

None split str

Optional. The split to load (e.g. "train", "test"). When None, the entire DatasetDict is iterated in split order.

None revision str

Optional. The dataset revision (commit hash, branch, tag).

None streaming bool

If True (default), use HF's IterableDataset so rows are downloaded on demand — required for datasets that don't fit on disk. The generator naturally terminates when the source is exhausted, so the trainer ends the epoch on its own; pass steps_per_epoch only if you also want shorter epochs.

True input_data_model DataModel

See Dataset.

None input_template str

See Dataset.

None output_data_model DataModel

See Dataset.

None output_template str

See Dataset.

None batch_size int

Examples per yielded batch. Defaults to 1.

1 limit int

Optional. See Dataset. Caps how many rows are consumed (across all splits). Also makes __len__ available for streaming datasets.

None **kwargs

Forwarded to datasets.load_dataset (e.g. data_files, token, trust_remote_code, ...).

{}

items.title: LocalDataset
items.text:
LocalDataset(path, *, format=None, input_data_model=None, input_schema=None, input_template=None, output_data_model=None, output_schema=None, output_template=None, batch_size=1, limit: int = None, repeat: int = 1)

Streaming dataset backed by a local file (JSON list, JSONL, CSV, or Parquet).

Format is auto-detected from path's extension unless format is set explicitly. Each row is a dict keyed by column name and is exposed as Jinja2 variables — same convention as HuggingFaceDataset.

Example:

ds = LocalDataset(
    path="data/eval.jsonl",
    input_template='{"messages":[{"role":"user","content": {{ question | tojson }}}]}',
    output_template='{"role":"assistant","content": {{ answer | tojson }}}',
    batch_size=8,
)
program.evaluate(x=ds)

Name Type Description Default path str

The filesystem path to the data file.

required format str

Optional. Override the auto-detected format. One of "json" (a file holding a list of records, or an object with one list in it), "jsonl", "csv", "parquet". Defaults to None (detect from extension).

None input_data_model DataModel

See Dataset. Defaults to ChatMessages.

None input_template str

See Dataset.

None output_data_model DataModel

See Dataset. Defaults to ChatMessage.

None output_template str

See Dataset.

None batch_size int

Examples per yielded batch. Defaults to 1.

1 limit int

Optional. See Dataset. Caps how many rows are consumed.

None

items.title: check
items.text:
check() -> int

Read the whole file and say what is wrong with it, before a run does; returns its row count.

Raises ValueError naming the file and the first bad line (jsonl) or row (csv): a line that is not JSON, a line that is not an object, a row with more values than the header, no rows at all.

items.title: FolderDataset
items.text:
FolderDataset(path, *, pattern='*', recursive=False, format=None, encoding='utf-8', input_data_model=None, input_schema=None, input_template=None, output_data_model=None, output_schema=None, output_template=None, batch_size=1, limit: int = None, repeat: int = 1)

Streaming dataset where each file in a folder is one record.

Files are read in deterministic alphabetical order and exposed to the Jinja2 templates as a flat dict. The schema depends on the file's format:

  • .json / .yaml / .yml files are parsed: if the parsed value is a dict, its keys are spread at the top level; otherwise it is exposed as record.
  • .txt / .md (and any other extension when format="text") are read as UTF-8 strings and exposed as text.

Every record additionally exposes filesystem metadata as _filename (full filename), _stem (filename without extension), and _path (path relative to the dataset root, posix-style).

Example:

ds = FolderDataset(
    path="data/cases",
    pattern="*.json",
    input_template='{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":{{ question | tojson }}}]}',
    output_template='{"role":"assistant","content":{{ answer | tojson }}}',
    batch_size=4,
)
program.evaluate(x=ds)

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The folder containing one file per record.

required pattern str

Glob pattern selecting which files inside path count as records. Defaults to "*" (everything at the top level). Combine with recursive=True for nested folders.

'*' recursive bool

If True, walk subfolders too (uses rglob with pattern). Defaults to False.

False format str

Optional. Override the auto-detected per-file format. One of "json", "yaml", "text". Defaults to None (detect from each file's extension).

None encoding str

Text encoding for file reads. Defaults to "utf-8".

'utf-8' input_data_model DataModel

See Dataset. Defaults to ChatMessages.

None input_template str

See Dataset.

None output_data_model DataModel

See Dataset. Defaults to ChatMessage.

None output_template str

See Dataset.

None batch_size int

Examples per yielded batch. Defaults to 1.

1 limit int

Optional. See Dataset. Caps how many files are consumed.

None

items.title: MLflowDataset
items.text:
MLflowDataset(name=None, *, dataset_id=None, tracking_uri=None, input_data_model=None, input_schema=None, input_template=None, output_data_model=None, output_schema=None, output_template=None, batch_size=1, limit=None, repeat=1)

An MLflow evaluation dataset.

Read from the arena's MLflow source server.

The arena keeps two MLflow servers apart: MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, where evaluation runs are traced, and MLFLOW_SOURCE_TRACKING_URI, where datasets (and traces to judge) are read from. The engine's loader only knows the former, so this subclass defaults tracking_uri to the latter; an explicit tracking_uri on the dataset still wins. Everything else — fields, templates, records — is the library's.

items.title: LangfuseDataset
items.text:
LangfuseDataset(dataset_name, *, version=None, streaming=True, page_size=50, input_data_model=None, input_schema=None, input_template=None, output_data_model=None, output_schema=None, output_template=None, batch_size=1, limit: int = None, repeat: int = 1)

Streaming dataset backed by a Langfuse dataset.

See https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/experiments/datasets. Each Langfuse DatasetItem exposes input, expected_output, metadata, and id; those names become the variables available to the Jinja2 input_template / output_template. Auth comes from env vars (LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY, LANGFUSE_HOST); set them in .env.

Example:

ds = LangfuseDataset(
    dataset_name="mmlu_subset",
    input_template='{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":{{ input | tojson }}}]}',
    output_template='{"role":"assistant","content":{{ expected_output | tojson }}}',
    batch_size=1,
)
program.evaluate(x=ds)

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default dataset_name str

The Langfuse dataset name (langfuse.get_dataset(name)).

required version str | datetime

Optional. The UTC point-in-time snapshot to pin items to (Langfuse datasets are versioned by timestamp, not by string tag — see Langfuse.get_dataset(version=...)). Accepts an ISO 8601 string ("2026-04-15T00:00:00Z"), a YAML timestamp (already parsed to datetime), or None for the latest state.

None streaming bool

If True (default), fetch items one page at a time as the dataset is iterated — items don't need to fit in memory and __len__ is unknown unless limit is set. If False, prefetch the entire dataset upfront via Langfuse.get_dataset(...).

True page_size int

Items per page request when streaming. Defaults to 50, matching the SDK's fetch_items_page_size default.

50 input_data_model DataModel

See Dataset. Defaults to ChatMessages.

None input_template str

See Dataset.

None output_data_model DataModel

See Dataset. Defaults to ChatMessage.

None output_template str

See Dataset.

None batch_size int

Examples per yielded batch. Defaults to 1.

1 limit int

Optional. See Dataset. Caps how many items are consumed.

None

items.title: LangSmithDataset
items.text:
LangSmithDataset(dataset_name, *, as_of=None, input_data_model=None, input_schema=None, input_template=None, output_data_model=None, output_schema=None, output_template=None, batch_size=1, limit: int = None, repeat: int = 1)

Streaming dataset backed by a LangSmith dataset.

See https://docs.smith.langchain.com/evaluation/concepts#datasets. ds = LangSmithDataset(
    dataset_name="mmlu_subset",

    output_template='{"role":"assistant","content":{{ outputs.answer | tojson }}}',
    batch_size=1,
)
program.evaluate(x=ds)

The LangSmith dataset name.

required as_of str | datetime

None input_data_model DataModel

See Dataset. Defaults to ChatMessages.

See Dataset.

See Dataset. Defaults to ChatMessage.

See Dataset.

items.title: UnityCatalogDataset
items.text:
UnityCatalogDataset(table, *, version=None, as_of=None, storage_path=None, read_batch_size=10000, input_data_model=None, input_schema=None, input_template=None, output_data_model=None, output_schema=None, output_template=None, batch_size=1, limit: int = None, repeat: int = 1)

Streaming dataset backed by a Unity Catalog (Databricks or OSS) table.

Each row in the target table becomes a raw dict whose keys are the column names. The _iter_rows() implementation resolves the table to its backing storage path (s3://…) via the Unity Catalog REST API, reads the Delta or Parquet data with deltalake + pyarrow, and streams rows without pulling the full table into memory first.

items.title: Auth & connectivity
items.text:
• UC REST API — read from UNITY_CATALOG_API_URL (must already include the /api/2.1/unity-catalog prefix) and bearer token UC_TOKEN.
  • S3 / object storage — reads from AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and optionally S3_ENDPOINT (for MinIO/Scaleway-compatible stores; region defaults to fr-par).

items.title: Resolution flow
items.text:
1. GET /tables/{catalog}.{schema}.{table} → storage_location (e.g. s3://bucket/path/to/table) and content_hash (the UC table version token).
  2. If version or as_of is given, it is forwarded to the Delta reader as a version integer or timestamp string.
  3. The Delta table is opened via deltalake.DeltaTable; if the path does not contain a _delta_log/ directory the reader falls back to plain Parquet via pyarrow.dataset.
  4. Rows are streamed in record-batch chunks (controlled by batch_size at the storage layer — distinct from the run's batch_size).

The resolved content_hash / storage_location are stored as self.metadata for downstream pinning / reproducibility logging.

Example YAML config::

datasets:
  uc_eval_set:
    type: unity_catalog
    table: my_catalog.eval_schema.questions_v2
    version: 3
    input_template: |
      {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": {{ question | tojson }}}]}
    output_template: |
      {"role": "assistant", "content": {{ reference_answer | tojson }}}
    batch_size: 8
    limit: 500

Python usage::

ds = UnityCatalogDataset(
    table="my_catalog.eval_schema.questions_v2",
    version=3,
    input_template='{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":{{ question | tojson }}}]}',
    batch_size=8,
)
program.evaluate(x=ds())

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default table str

Fully-qualified table name in catalog.schema.table form. Required.

required version int

Optional. Pin the Delta table to this numeric version. Mutually exclusive with as_of.

None as_of str

Optional. Pin the Delta table to a UTC timestamp string (ISO 8601, e.g. "2026-04-15T00:00:00Z"). Mutually exclusive with version.

None storage_path str

Optional explicit s3://… path override. When given, the UC REST lookup is skipped entirely.

None read_batch_size int

Number of rows per Arrow record batch when streaming the Delta/Parquet source. Defaults to 10_000. Distinct from the run's batch_size.

10000 input_data_model

See :class:~src.datasets.dataset.Dataset.

items.title: Configuration entries
items.text: One model per registry entry: what a configs/<registry>.yaml entry may hold. Each refuses a field it does not know.

items.title: ModelEntry
items.text: A models.<name>: entry.

items.title: RewardEntry
items.text: A rewards.<name>: entry: a catalog reward (type), its constructor kwargs (config), which way is better.

items.title: block property
items.text:
block: dict[str, Any]

The spec rewards.get builds it from: {name, direction, ...config}.

items.title: DatasetEntry
items.text: A datasets.<name>: entry: a provider (type, config, with the row's Jinja templates), what answers each row, the reward that scores it.

items.title: to_entry
items.text:
to_entry() -> dict[str, Any]

The flat mapping the dataset providers read (config.flatten_dataset).

items.title: AgentBlock
items.text:
A dataset's agent: block: a FunctionCallingAgent over the MCP servers it names.

Every other key (max_iterations, autonomous, instructions, ...) flows to FunctionCallingAgent.

items.title: HarborBlock
items.text:
A dataset's harbor: block: each row a Harbor task, done by an agent the model under test drives in a sandbox.

Two sources of tasks. A dataset of type: harbor_tasks reads Harbor task folders as they are (task.toml, instruction.md, environment/, tests/, solution/), one row each, and runs each with Harbor's verifier: its tests/ score it, and the harbor_verifier reward reads that score. Any other dataset names an environment: each row's input_template renders its question, which, after instructions, is the instruction.md of a task generated from that environment, whose default tests/ collects the agent's answer for the dataset's reward to score on the arena's side.

What the agent did is the prediction, Harbor's own ATIF trajectory (HarborTrajectory), with its answer: what it wrote to answer_file (an agent that works a terminal acts rather than replies), else its last message; and, for a task with its own tests, the verifier's rewards.

items.title: MetricEntry
items.text:
One entry of a metrics: list (an evaluation's or a dataset's).

Written as a bare string (- total_tokens) or a mapping with class: plus an optional alias: / direction: / objective: and any constructor kwargs; the string is read as {class: ...}. Without direction:, a measurement of what the calls spend (cost, total_tokens, avg_latency, ...) is better lower and anything else higher (metric_direction).

items.title: kwargs property
items.text:
kwargs: dict[str, Any]

Extra fields forwarded as constructor kwargs (incl. name:).

items.title: McpServerEntry
items.text: An mcp_servers.<name>: entry: what a dataset's agent.mcp_servers names.

items.title: A2aAgentEntry
items.text: An a2a_agents.<name>: entry: what an a2a sweep's axis names.

items.title: EnvironmentEntry
items.text: An environments.<name>: entry: a Harbor task environment.

items.title: HealthcheckSpec
items.text: A command Harbor runs in the container until it succeeds: [environment.healthcheck].

items.title: EvaluationEntry
items.text: An evaluations.<name>: entry: a saved sweep.

items.title: LeaderboardEntry
items.text:
A leaderboards.<name>: entry: a scope, and each metric's share of the score.

Empty datasets / models mean every one scored; empty shares the default preset (leaderboard.default_shares).

items.title: Budget
items.text: A hard limit on one metric of a leaderboard: a model breaking it is left out of the ranking, and listed as such.

items.title: run_sweep async
items.text:
run_sweep(config_path: str, *, no_cache: bool = False, verbose: int = 0, state_dir: Path = DEFAULT_STATE_DIR, on_event: Callable[[dict], None] | None = None, on_sample: Callable[[dict], None] | None = None, samples_per_cell: int = 0, batch_size: int | None = None, mlflow_experiment: str | None = None, mlflow_tracking_uri: str | None = None, mlflow_tags: dict | None = None) -> dict

Run the full sweep and return the JSON-serializable result dict.

on_event, when given, receives progress dicts as the sweep advances: sweep_start (models, datasets), dataset_start, dataset_resumed (models already scored / queued for a retry, only when a previous attempt left state behind), dataset_ready (batches), cell_start (model), batch (batch, batches_total, running reward), cell_end (metrics), dataset_end (statuses per model) and sweep_end. Raising SweepCancelled from it aborts the sweep.

on_sample, with samples_per_cell > 0, receives the first rows of each (model, dataset) cell as {dataset, model, index, input, target, output} — what the model was asked and what it answered, which the aggregate matrix throws away. Rows are numbered in dataset order, so the same index is the same row for every model.

mlflow_experiment, when given (and observability is enabled), attaches an MLflow Monitor callback that logs each trial's evaluate metrics as one run of that experiment, tagged with mlflow_tags, the dataset and the model. Without it the framework still adds its default Monitor, which files metrics under an experiment named after the program.

Programmatic entry point (e.g. for an API endpoint that needs the matrix without going through stdout). One GridSearch tuner runs per dataset over Choice("language_model", ...) — model is the only HP axis; the dataset is a fixed search context. Each tuner persists trial state under <state_dir>/<dataset>/ (default .open-arena, override with state_dir), the same cache the CLI reads, and distinct state_dirs never collide.

That cache is also what makes a sweep resumable: point a new call at the state_dir of an interrupted one (with no_cache=False, which is the default) and every cell that completed is skipped — its scores are read back from the trial — while the cells that failed or were in flight are re-run along with the ones never reached. Programs are only built for the cells that still have to run. See _resume_grid.

Programs are built eagerly per (model, dataset) cell, then the cells run in turn, model-major, on this event loop (_run_cell), each with a view of its dataset batched to the run's batch_size (else the dataset's own): the batch is what the framework sends at once.

A cell that cannot give a score ends FAILED (or INVALID) with why, and the other cells still run: an agent whose MCP servers gave no tools, a cell none of whose rows got an answer (_NoAnswerGuard), any error raised while it ran. A row that alone got no answer scores 0 and the cell goes on. The result's rows carry each cell's status.

no_cache=True drops every per-dataset cache before starting — use it when the model list or any dataset's reward / metric set changed. It is also what makes a run un-resumable, so a resume must never set it. verbose is forwarded to Program.evaluate (0 silent, 1 progress bar, 2 per-batch).

items.title: harbor
items.text:
An environment entry, written the way a Harbor task holds it, and what the arena knows of Harbor.

A Harbor task is a folder: task.toml, instruction.md, environment/, tests/ (run by Harbor's verifier after the agent, writing /logs/verifier/reward.txt or reward.json), solution/ (run by the oracle agent), and optionally steps/. A workspace's own tasks are such folders (type: harbor_tasks datasets run them, scored by their tests). An environments.<name>: entry is the sandbox part of a task generated from rows, task.toml's [environment] section (with its healthcheck and mcp_servers) and, when the entry builds its image, environment/Dockerfile. task_files returns both, for a task to be assembled around them.

An MCP server is passed as its connection (McpServerSpec.connection()); Harbor reads stdio, sse and streamable-http, so a websocket server is refused. Harbor's server entry is only a name, a transport and a command or URL: a connection that needs headers (a key) or a stdio env / cwd would reach the agent without them, so it is refused too. A stdio command runs inside the sandbox, so the image must hold it.

Every trial runs Harbor's verifier. A task folder's own tests score it; a task generated from rows gets the arena's default tests, which collect the agent's answer for the dataset's reward to score on the arena's side. What the agent did is read back from its ATIF trajectory (trajectory_messages, final_answer) into the prediction, HarborTrajectory. agents() says where each agent runs and which provider it calls, agent_problem refuses a model or a network it cannot work with, and sandbox_capabilities / environment_problems an entry a sandbox provider cannot start.

items.title: agents
items.text:
agents() -> list[dict[str, Any]]

Each agent a harbor: block may name: {name, runs, provider, params}.

runs is host (it calls the model from the arena, typing into the sandbox) or sandbox (it is installed in the sandbox and calls the model from there); provider the one provider it calls, or None for any; params the model settings it takes of temperature, reasoning_effort and max_tokens.

items.title: agent_problem
items.text:
agent_problem(agent: str, model_id: str, environment: EnvironmentSpec | None) -> str | None

Why agent cannot work with model_id in environment (None: a task folder's own, not known here), as one sentence, or None.

An agent bound to a provider calls only its models; one installed in the sandbox calls its model from there, so it needs the network, and a model served from the arena's machine is out of its reach.

items.title: environment_problems
items.text:
environment_problems(spec: EnvironmentSpec, sandbox: str) -> list[str]

What of spec sandbox provider sandbox cannot give, one sentence each: every trial would fail on it.

items.title: task_files
items.text:
task_files(spec: EnvironmentSpec, servers: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] | None = None) -> dict[str, str]

{path in the task folder: content}: the task.toml section, and environment/Dockerfile when one is built.

items.title: leaderboard
items.text:
Leaderboards: the scores of finished runs, gathered and ranked.

Two steps, the same two the web app takes:

  1. board(runs) gathers the latest cell per (model, dataset) from sweep results, newest run first, the way /leaderboard does: a cell is taken whole from one run, its reward plus every metric that run recorded, and eol_days is added to every cell of a model.
  2. rank(board, ...) scores the models of a leaderboard's scope, the port of the frontend's lib/criteria.ts: each metric normalized per dataset to [FLOOR, 1] against the models in scope (linear for the reward and eol_days, log for magnitudes), combined as a weighted geometric mean, and averaged over the datasets. A model must be scored on every dataset in scope, and a metric only carries weight when every cell in scope records it. The Pareto frontier is marked over the weighted metrics.

Plain dicts in and out, so the CLI prints them and a caller can dump them.

items.title: board
items.text:
board(runs: list[dict], *, today: date | None = None, eol: bool = True) -> dict

The leaderboard over runs, each {"id", "result": <run_sweep result>, "model_ids": {name: id}}, newest first.

The one aggregation: the backend's /leaderboard and openarena leaderboards run both read the board from here. A row's model is what the board reports; model_ids maps it to the id it called, for eol_days and the entry's model_id (the name itself when absent).

Returns {"datasets", "metrics", "entries"}, entries being {"model", "model_id", "scores": {dataset: {"value", "direction", "run_id", "metrics": {name: {"value", "direction"}}}}, "mean"}, best mean first. eol off leaves eol_days out (it asks the outside world).

items.title: rank
items.text:
rank(data: dict, *, datasets: list[str] | None = None, models: list[str] | None = None, shares: dict[str, float] | None = None, budgets: list[dict] | None = None, group_shares: dict[str, float] | None = None, dataset_shares: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> dict

Rank the models of the scope, as the leaderboard page does.

datasets / models empty or None mean everything the board has, as in a saved leaderboard. shares are percents per metric; a share on a metric the scope only partly records is dropped, and none at all means the default preset. group_shares / dataset_shares weigh the datasets (dataset_weights); one at 0 is out of the score and not required. Returns {"datasets", "models", "shares", "axes", "rows", "skipped", "gaps", "excluded"}: rows best first, each {"rank", "model", "score", "values", "contributions", "per_dataset", "dataset_contributions", "on_frontier", "runs"}; skipped the models in scope left unranked and gaps why, per model a list of {"dataset", "missing"} (missing None: never scored there).

budgets are hard limits, {"metric", "op": "lte" | "gte", "value"}: a model breaking one on any dataset is left out before anything is normalized, so it cannot stretch the scale of the ones kept, and comes back in excluded, {"model", "failed": [budget, ...]}.

items.title: default_shares
items.text:
default_shares(metrics: list[str]) -> dict[str, float]

The page's default preset, "Reward first": the reward high, the other measurements low, model facts off.

items.title: normalize
items.text:
normalize(name: str, direction: str, values: list[float]) -> list[float]

One metric column to [FLOOR, 1], higher better: linear for LINEAR, else log when every value is positive.

items.title: pareto_frontier
items.text:
pareto_frontier(points: dict[str, dict[str, float]], axes: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> set[str]

The ids no other point dominates: at least as good on every axis and strictly better on one.

items.title: Rewards
items.text: The catalog a reward's type names, and the rewards openarena adds to it.

items.title: rewards
items.text:
Reward registry + YAML resolver.

Combines the framework's built-in Reward subclasses (auto-discovered via the framework's reward registry) with the project-local rewards the framework has no equivalent of (MultiJudgePanel, AnswerAccuracy, RetrievalRecall, ToolCallsAccuracy) into a single _REWARD_TYPES map keyed by the reward's snake_case class name. The rubrics, agent, recursive and deep judges that used to live here ship with the framework since 0.10. get(spec) instantiates a reward from either a string name ("exact_match") or a YAML-shaped dict; string language_model: / embedding_model: values flow straight into the reward constructor — the framework resolves them via language_models.get / embedding_models.get — and a {model, ...params} mapping (a models.yaml entry with params) is built into that model first.

items.title: get
items.text:
get(spec, **kwargs)

Resolve a reward spec into an instantiated rewards.Reward.

spec can be: - A string snake_case reward name, e.g. "exact_match". - A dict shaped like the YAML config: 

name: lm_as_judge
language_model: ollama/llama3.2
instructions: |
  ...
Every key besides name is forwarded as a kwarg to the reward constructor. String language_model: / embedding_model: values pass through verbatim — the framework resolves them into concrete LanguageModel / EmbeddingModel instances on demand. A model given as a mapping, {model: openai/gpt-4o, temperature: 0.0} (what Config resolves a models.yaml entry with params to), is built here with those params. An answer_fields: list scopes the reward to those top-level fields (AnswerFields).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default spec

Snake_case name or config dict (see above).

required **kwargs

Extra constructor kwargs, merged on top of any in spec.

{}

Raises:

Type Description KeyError

If no reward is registered under the resolved name.

items.title: accepted_kwargs
items.text:
accepted_kwargs(name: str) -> set[str]

The config keys the reward registered as name takes: its named constructor kwargs, less the hidden ones, plus the masks.

items.title: category
items.text:
category(name: str) -> str

How the reward registered as name scores: rubrics_judge, agent_judge, lm_judge or deterministic.

A named override, else its base class, else what it calls out to: a deterministic reward compares by rule or by embedding, with no judge.

items.text:

Grade each field of the answer with the deterministic metric that fits its type, and average.
